R0276.title: Robot Physical Harm & Functional-Safety Failure
R0276.definition: Functional-safety incidents where control failure, force-control anomaly, e-stop bypass, or collaborative-robot safety-function failure causes the robot to inflict physical harm on people or the environment.
R0276.description:
Robot physical harm & functional-safety failure is a lethal risk unique to embodied intelligence versus pure software security. The Knightscope K5 security robot (1.5 m tall, 136 kg) knocked down a 16-month-old toddler at a Stanford shopping center in 2016 and fell into a fountain in 2017. In 2015 a technician at the Volkswagen Baunatal plant was crushed to death by an industrial robot inside a safety guardrail. In 2019 a worker at a Guangdong Weijie hardware workshop was struck in the head and killed by a robot. In 2026 a humanoid robot knocked down an elderly person during a performance at a Chengdu mall. For cobots, IOActive showed that a UR5 even at 5 kg payload and low speed is strong enough to break a human skull and can be remotely disabled from its e-stop. This risk is governed by functional-safety standards including ISO 10218 (industrial-robot safety), ISO/TS 15066 (collaborative robots), and ISO 13482 (personal-care robots).

This risk relates to R0179 (industrial IoT security risk), but is specialized for robot physical harm and functional safety, emphasizing personal safety and standards compliance.
R0276.influence: Directly causes casualties, property damage, and product recalls; it is a lethal risk unique to embodied intelligence versus pure software security, governed by ISO 10218/ISO/TS 15066 functional-safety standards, with significant accident-liability disputes.
